newsitem.title: ITALY: U.N. seeks funds to feed Iraqis ahead of oil deal.
newsitem.headline: U.N. seeks funds to feed Iraqis ahead of oil deal.

text.p: The U.N. World Food Programme on Tuesday asked governments for money to feed hungry people in Iraq until a United Nations food-for-oil deal becomes fully operational.
The Rome-based agency said it had asked donors for $54 million in order to feed 2.1 million Iraqis until March.
The WFP, the U.N.'s food aid arm, said it was reaching only about 700,000 hungry people in Iraq because of a lack of funds.
The food-for-oil agreement between the U.N. and Baghdad came into effect on December 10 and allows Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil over six months to buy humanitarian supplies for its people.
The WFP said in a statement that it was not clear whether food bought under the agreement would reach people in need before the end of the harsh Iraqi winter.
"Iraqis, expecially in the centre and south of the country, desperately need our help," Mona Hammam, WFP's regional director for the Mediterranean and Middle East, was quoted as saying.
